_comment: Task 2b targeted negatives, driven by the diagnosis. C_wide_uniform's false positives on the noscreen probe concentrate in indoor office, meeting and home environments with textless screen-like surfaces, driven by brightness and screen-like rectangles, and inversely correlated with faces. These add that class of environment and blank screen-like surface.
_label: category=negative_clean, which prepare_dataset maps to label 0 (do not record). Each new slug becomes a subclass under negative_clean. This phase does not run prepare_dataset and does not merge them into the training pool.
_design: Deliberately weighted toward empty, blank, off and textless, plus daylight, bright and window, for three reasons: attack the false-trigger cue (bright indoors plus a screen-like rectangle) rather than the scene label; keep the chance of pulling in a readable text screen, which would be a positive, low; and match the finding that false positives are brighter by +0.186.
_distinct_from_task2: Different from the 14 people categories in keywords_task2_neg_people.json, which deliberately avoided office and meeting scenes. This round covers exactly the indoor built environment task 2 left out and the model is getting wrong. The slugs do not collide with the 28 existing negative subclasses.
_methodology_tension: These scenes are the same type as the noscreen probe (office, meeting room, living room), so putting them into training demotes the probe on those scenes from a generalisation test to an in-distribution one. That is a phase-two methodological trade-off and is still to be decided.
_manual_qc: Before they enter training, manually remove any image containing readable screen, whiteboard, document, slide or code-screen text. Removal goes through the guard script's quarantine, which moves rather than deletes, so it stays traceable.
